question: Where does a community midwife mainly work?

options.A: Exclusively in private urban maternity homes
options.C: Within rural and grassroots health clinics

explanation: Community midwives work in local communities and primary care centers to bring healthcare closer to families. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T2#BMP215_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why is the role of a community midwife so important for Nigeria's healthcare?

options.A: It guarantees free medical care for every citizen in the country
options.B: It completely replaces the need for doctors in all hospitals
options.C: It focuses on grassroots prevention and reducing maternal deaths
options.D: It eliminates traditional birth attendants entirely from society

explanation: The main goal is to provide accessible, preventative care locally to help lower maternal and newborn mortality rates. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T2#BMP215_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which tool does a community midwife commonly use during labor to check on progress?
explanation: The partograph is a standard, low-cost paper tool used to track labor progress and the well-being of mother and baby. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T2#BMP215_U1_T2_h2)

question: A woman visits the primary health clinic for a postnatal checkup. What should the midwife mainly check?

options.A: Visual acuity and blood cholesterol lipid profiles
options.B: Surgical site infection from a previous appendectomy
options.C: Range of motion in the lower lumbar spine joints
options.D: Uterine involution, lochia, and breastfeeding success

explanation: Postnatal checks focus on how the mother's body is recovering, checking lochia, and ensuring breastfeeding is going well. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T2#BMP215_U1_T2_h2)

question: What is a main goal of community mobilization efforts by a midwife?

options.A: To make health a shared community responsibility
options.B: To replace traditional rulers with health workers
options.C: To collect taxes for local government clinics
options.D: To enforce strict fines for missing antenatal visits

explanation: Mobilization encourages the whole community to take an active role in supporting maternal and child health. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T2#BMP215_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why do community midwives need to educate the public outside of the clinic walls?

options.A: Because pregnant women are forbidden from entering health facilities
options.B: Because clinical equipment is too expensive to use inside the building
options.C: To fulfill mandatory administrative hours required by the government
options.D: To ensure health messages reach people within their own cultural context

explanation: Going outside the clinic lets the midwife meet families where they live and talk to them in spaces familiar to them. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T2#BMP215_U1_T2_h3)

question: What does maternal and child health advocacy mainly involve for a community midwife?

options.A: Speaking up for vulnerable women and demanding better care
options.B: Financing the construction of large urban hospitals
options.C: Importing foreign medical drugs without government permits
options.D: Serving as a legal defense attorney in court trials

explanation: Advocacy involves standing up for the rights of mothers and newborns to make sure they get fair and compassionate treatment. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T2#BMP215_U1_T2_h4)

question: How can a community midwife practice advocacy at the local clinic level?

options.A: By keeping all health budget information strictly confidential
options.B: By refusing to treat patients who cannot speak English
options.C: By discouraging women from seeking care outside the village
options.D: By demanding prompt attention for obstetric emergencies without delay

explanation: At the facility level, advocacy means pushing past delays so life-saving emergencies are handled immediately. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T2#BMP215_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which health workers do community midwives often partner with for everyday primary care tasks?
explanation: CHEWs and community midwives work closely together in primary health centers on tasks like immunizations and health education. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T2#BMP215_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why is it encouraged for community midwives to engage with traditional birth attendants (TBAs)?

options.A: To teach them danger sign recognition and improve referral pathways
options.B: To hand over all clinical responsibilities to them permanently
options.C: To convince them to stop practicing medicine altogether
options.D: To help them set up private commercial pharmacy shops

explanation: Working with TBAs helps spot pregnancy complications early and gets mothers safely referred to skilled care when needed. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T2#BMP215_U1_T2_h5)

question: How should a community midwife handle a harmful traditional pregnancy practice?

options.A: Publicly mock the family to deter others in the village
options.B: Negotiate safely around the practice while respecting the people
options.C: Refuse to provide any further medical care to the household
options.D: Ignore it completely since traditions cannot be influenced

explanation: Showing respect and using gentle health education builds trust, making families much more open to changing unsafe customs. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T2#BMP215_U1_T2_h6)

question: What common challenge do community midwives often face in rural clinics?

options.A: Too many operational ambulances stationed at the clinic
options.B: An overabundance of surgical specialists on site
options.C: Excessive amounts of high-tech laboratory equipment
options.D: Constant shortages of essential drugs and reliable electricity

explanation: Rural primary clinics in Nigeria frequently deal with basic infrastructure problems and running out of key medications. [learn more](BMP215_U1_T2#BMP215_U1_T2_h6)
